cmad.notes: SDO is operational (launched 2010-02-11, no StopDate) and NASA-funded (first Living With a Star mission) -> a CMAD is expected. An EVE CMAD was located in the NASA LWS SOMA document repository (Document No. EVE-T-11003, Rev. A, 2005-01-31; a Rev B copy also exists at https://scholar.colorado.edu/concern/defaults/db78tf06d). Front page: 'Prepared By: Francis G. Eparvier, EVE Project Scientist'; revision-history approver initials 'TNW' = Thomas N. Woods (EVE PI). Both are Strong current-team evidence for the EVE instrument. No separate AIA or HMI CMAD was located (probed sibling filenames in the same SOMA path and general web search -- none surfaced); those instruments' current teams were drawn from SPASE Contacts + instrument papers instead. An SDO 2020 Senior Review Proposal (http://hmi.stanford.edu/papers/SDO_SR_2020_assembled_3.pdf) also names the current team but is not a CMAD.

instrument_coverage.notes: Observatory record has no downward instrument links; reverse-lookup of https://spase-metadata.org/SMWG/Instrument/SDO/ returned AIA, EVE, HMI and each record's ObservatoryID confirms spase://SMWG/Observatory/SDO. External ground truth (SDO overview paper Pesnell et al. 2012 and the record's own Description) enumerates exactly three payload instruments: AIA, EVE, HMI. SPASE roster is complete -- no instruments missing. This is an Observatory record, so all three instruments' leads are legitimate candidates.

notes: Operating span: the SDO Observatory record carries no explicit OperatingSpan/StartDate element. Start set to launch date 2010-02-11 (from the record Description); mission is still operational so stop = null. Downstream era-matching should use this launch-anchored span.

Observatory overview paper (Pesnell, Thompson, Chamberlin 2012, doi:10.1007/s11207-011-9841-3): only 3 authors, not alphabetized (Pesnell->Thompson->Chamberlin not sorted); all three taken as Strong (positions 1-3). Selection confident: exact title match 'The Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)', heavily cited, published 2012 near operations start.

AIA paper (Lemen et al. 2012, n=47): partially alphabetized. Backward scan finds a long sorted suffix beginning at author 3 (Akin, Boerner, Chou, Drake, Duncan, ...), so prefix = Lemen, Title (2 authors). Took ONLY Lemen and Title as Strong-tier; Akin and the rest of the sorted tail carry no position evidence (Akin recorded as excluded to show the tail was evaluated, not dropped). Selection confident: the AIA SPASE record itself links this DOI as 'The SDO/AIA Instrument paper'.

HMI paper (Scherrer et al. 2012, n=13): NOT alphabetized -- backward scan sorted suffix = {Schrijver, Tarbell, Tomczyk} = 3 (< 5 threshold). Position signals contribution: took first 5 weighted -- Scherrer/Schou/Bush Strong (1-3), Kosovichev/Bogart Medium (4-5). Selection confident: exact HMI-investigation title match, 2012, near operations start.

EVE paper (Woods et al. 2010, n=18): partially alphabetized. Backward scan sorted suffix = {Bailey, Fuller-Rowell, Sojka, Tobiska, Viereck} = 5 (exactly at threshold), prefix = positions 1-13. Applied prefix positional weighting only through position 5: Woods/Eparvier/Hock Strong (1-3), Jones/Woodraska Medium (4-5). Prefix members beyond position 5 (Judge, Didkovsky, Lean, Mariska, Warren, McMullin, Chamberlin, Berthiaume) not taken on position alone; McMullin recorded as excluded as a representative of that group. Note Chamberlin (prefix #12) is independently Strong via the mission overview paper.

CMAD: an EVE CMAD (EVE-T-11003 Rev A, 2005) was located in the NASA LWS SOMA repository and gives Strong current-team evidence for Eparvier (prepared) and Woods (approver 'TNW'). No AIA or HMI CMAD was located despite filename probing in the same SOMA path and web search -- current AIA/HMI teams rest on SPASE Contacts + instrument papers. Reviewer should note the AIA/HMI CMAD gap.

AIA current PI in SPASE Contacts is Meng Jin (Medium); FormerPIs Cheung, Schrijver, Title are qualifying-role Medium. This captures two PI generations for AIA (original team via the Lemen paper prefix + FormerPIs; current PI Meng Jin). Both generations are legitimate for an Observatory record.

SMWG Person registry: existing records found for Pesnell, Thompson, Meng Jin, Cheung, Karel Schrijver, Title, Woods, Scherrer, Lemen. No Person record for Chamberlin (both P.C./Phillip.C variants 404), Schou, Bush, Kosovichev, Bogart, Eparvier, Hock, Jones, Woodraska -- ids left null, not drafted.

Provider team page (https://sdo.gsfc.nasa.gov/mission/project.php) did not expose a structured, machine-readable team roster (org chart is an image); mission-level roles were therefore taken from the overview paper and the Observatory Contacts (Pesnell, ProjectScientist).
